claims.text: The proposed untreated material is an as-cast refractory high-entropy alloy such as Mo-Nb-Ta-W-V.
Approximately 5 atomic% aluminum is to be incorporated into the refractory high-entropy alloy.
Mechanical alloying or co-melting can be used to incorporate the aluminum.
Adding approximately 5 atomic% aluminum will promote formation of an alumina surface scale.
The aluminum-induced alumina scale will be stable and adherent at high temperature in an oxidizing environment.
A uniform distribution of aluminum in the alloy will facilitate formation of a continuous protective aluminum-oxide scale.
At elevated temperature in an oxygen-containing environment, aluminum will preferentially oxidize to Al2O3.
The resulting dense Al2O3 barrier will limit oxygen diffusion into the alloy.
Limiting oxygen diffusion will reduce oxygen ingress and subsequent oxidation damage.
At approximately 1200°C in air for 24 hours, the aluminum-modified alloy will have at least 20% less mass gain than the untreated alloy.
At approximately 1200°C in air for 24 hours, the aluminum-modified alloy will develop a thinner oxide scale than the untreated alloy.
The untreated refractory high-entropy alloy typically experiences greater mass gain and deeper oxygen ingress.
The major protective benefit is expected above approximately 1000–1200°C in strongly oxidizing environments.
Insufficient aluminum content may prevent formation of a stable alumina layer.
Lower temperatures may prevent formation of a stable alumina layer.
The aluminum concentration and processing conditions needed to obtain a continuous alumina layer without compromising mechanical properties remain uncertain.
